terms.meaning: A single statement the AI makes, which must be backed by one or more facts.
A check that each claim is supported by known facts, and rejects it if not.
A safe, fixed sentence used when AI output is rejected.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports verifier and fixed cutoff
sections.what: Brings in the claim verifier, the claim and fact types, the AI provider classes and the verified generation function, and sets a fixed snapshot cutoff time.
sections.why: Likely reason: the tests use the same functions the app uses, so they check real verification behaviour.
sections.watch_out: The cutoff is fixed, so facts or claims dated after it may be excluded in these tests.

sections.name: facts, claim
sections.title: Shared facts and claim helper
sections.what: Sets up a small fixed set of match facts, including runs, balls, a model estimate, a derived value and one late event, plus a helper that builds a claim for the tests. Together these give every check the same known inputs.
sections.why: Fixed inputs make the checks predictable, so a failure points to the rule being tested and not to changing data.
sections.watch_out: The fact values and the cutoff time must stay consistent with the expectations below, or many tests fail at once.

sections.name: claim verifier
sections.title: Checks on claim verification
sections.what: Confirms that properly sourced claims are accepted, including small rounding differences. Confirms that OBSERVED and DERIVED claims without sources, unknown source ids, numbers not found in the cited facts, and events after the snapshot cutoff are all rejected.
sections.why: Likely reason: the app shows text generated by a language model, and these rules stop invented or future facts from reaching users.
sections.watch_out: The rounding tolerance and cutoff date comparison are the fragile parts. A loosened rule there would let fabricated numbers pass.

sections.name: claim verifier: banned content
sections.title: Checks on banned wording
sections.what: Confirms that betting, prize, secret and prompt-echo phrases are rejected, even when they are editorial text with no sources. A sentence that only mentions money in a disclaimer is also rejected.
sections.why: Likely reason: the product must not show gambling-style language or leak secrets and internal instructions to users.
sections.watch_out: The protection is only as broad as the phrases listed, so new wording needs new test cases.

sections.name: verified generation with template fallback
sections.title: Generation with fallback to a template
sections.what: Confirms that a verified model answer is kept, that a model answer with a made-up number is replaced by the plain template text, and that a broken template raises an error instead of being shown.
sections.why: Users should see either checked model text or the safe template, and a broken template should be found, not hidden.
sections.watch_out: The fallback test depends on the template still producing text that passes verification.
